observations: Photo 0 and 2 show a pulled engine (top-down view) with a dark plastic engine cover, red fuel injector/rail covers, attached to what looks like a transmission and front subframe with coilover struts on each side, sitting on wet, dirty pavement in an open yard.

Photo 1 shows the same or similar engine/transmission unit from a different angle, with another coil spring/hub assembly, a driveshaft stub, and other dismantled engines and parts stacked in the background.

A semi-transparent watermark reads 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' across the engine cover in all three photos - this is the seller's business name/watermark, not a legible part number or brand plate on the engine itself.
No engine casting number, VIN tag, build plate, or any legible manufacturer marking is visible on the engine block, transmission case, or cover in any photo.
The parts appear used/pulled (oily, dirty, some surface corrosion on the transmission case and subframe), consistent with a salvage yard environment.
No photo shows the engine running, no compression test, no dipstick/oil check, no close-up of any ID sticker or sticker on the engine cover.

identity.kind: used car engine with transmission and front suspension struts (pulled assembly)

claims.claim: We also deals on all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business statement; not shown or contradicted by any photo.

risks.risk: Make, model and engine displacement cannot be confirmed, which is the single biggest driver of this part's value.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine ID/casting number, the VIN sticker on the engine or firewall tag, or a clear shot of any OEM part number stamped on the block/transmission.
risks.if_unproven: cannot be priced at all without this - value swings enormously by make/model.

risks.risk: Mechanical condition unknown - could be a running take-out or a non-functional parts-only unit.
risks.proof: Video of the engine cranking/running, or at minimum a compression test readout.

risks.risk: Mileage and reason for removal (accident, flood, engine failure) unknown.
risks.proof: Odometer photo from donor vehicle or seller's invoice/import paperwork showing mileage and origin.

risks.risk: Completeness of the assembly (sensors, wiring harness, ECU, turbo if applicable) cannot be confirmed from these angles.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photos/video of the assembly listing all attached components.
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare engine/transmission only, excluding ancillary parts.

risks.risk: Exposure to rain/wet pavement in photos raises corrosion/water-ingress concern for electrical and internal components.
risks.proof: Close-up of connectors, intake, and any rust on internal-facing surfaces.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming moisture exposure risk, as-is condition.

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the engine ID plate, casting number, or VIN sticker to confirm make/model/displacement.
Video of the engine running or at least cranking.
Full set of photos showing all sides of the assembly and any accompanying parts (wiring, sensors, turbo).
Any paperwork on mileage/origin of the donor vehicle.
response.reason: The photos show a used engine/transmission/suspension assembly but no readable make, model, or displacement marking anywhere, and this identity is essential to set even a worst-case price for an engine part.
